source_title: Search underway for 12 people missing in landslide-hit southern Odisha village
source_excerpt: Bhubaneswar/Phulbani The Odisha government launched a search operation for 12 people who went missing after a rain-triggered landslide struck a village bordering Ganjam and Kandhamal districts a day ago, officials said on Saturday (October 31, 2026). Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P. Patil said altogether, 170 personnel of the National Disaster Response Force, Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force and Special Operation Group have been engaged in the operation to locate the missing people. Post-Arnab cyclone, heavy rain wreaks havoc in Odisha’s Ganjam, Gajapati districts Post-Arnab cyclone, heavy rain wreaks havoc in Odisha’s Ganjam, Gajapati districts More than 200 villages in 22 blocks across Ganjam and Gajapati districts severely affected; roads washed away, villages marooned and three rivers are in spate Post-Arnab cyclone, heavy rain wreaks havoc in Odisha’s Ganjam, Gajapati districts storyline 1 “A hilltop village was home to 26 people. Thirteen of them managed to escape from the landslide, while 13 others went missing. One of the missing people has been traced, and others are still untraceable. The search operation has been going on since Friday (October 30, 2026) night,” Mr. Patil told reporters on Saturday (October 31, 2026). The landslide at Gidipabali village under the Baibali panchayat in Ganjam's Bhanjanagar block was among the 10 such incidents that occurred during incessant rain triggered by cyclone Arnab. Heavy rain inundated hundreds of villages in the State’s southern part. Three people, including a nine-month-old baby, died in a landslide in Kandhamal district on Friday (October 30, 2026), while a person was found dead in Gajapati, the special relief commissioner said. 3 persons die in landslide as flood situation remains grim in Odisha storyline 1 Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said rescue and relief operations have been intensified in flood-affected districts, including Ganjam, with the safety and well-being of people given top priority. The administration and rescue teams remain actively engaged in providing all possible assistance to those affected," Mr. Majhi said in a social media post. Taking to X, Leader of Opposition Naveen Patnaik said he was "deeply saddened to learn of the tragic incident of landslides in Odisha's Kandhamal district due to the impact of cyclone Arnnab, resulting in the loss of several lives and many people going missing". "I urge the government to swiftly ensure all necessary steps are taken for the rescue of the people and to facilitate the restoration of normal life," he said. The thirteen people who managed to escape the landslide at Gidipabali village took shelter at a relief centre near G. Udaygiri of Kandhamal. Kandhamal District Collector Vedbhusan said two children are among them. According to one of the survivors, a huge mass of sludge cascaded down the hills, burying houses and leaving the entire village devastated. But they could not reach here,” said Rinima Mallik at the relief centre. Another survivor Soudamini Mallik said some of her relatives remain missing and requested the administration to save their lives. "All those who survived had sustained injuries after being hit by the stones," she claimed. G. Udayagiri Block Development Officer Satyanarayan Mishra said the two injured women — Samita Mallik and Manima Pradhan — have been shifted to a health centre. Ganjam District Collector V. Keerthi Vasan said relief work has been expedited in Aska and other parts of the district. “The overall situation is improving in Aska with coordinated efforts to restore normalcy," the Collector said, adding that 10 drinking water tankers and around 30,000 bottles were distributed till Friday (October 30, 2026) evening.
